newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain offshore banking units' H1 assets drop.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain offshore banking units' H1 assets drop.

text.p: Total assets of offshore banking units (OBUs) operating in Bahrain fell to $61.50 billion in the first half of 1996 from $67.98 billion a year earlier, official figures showed on Tuesday.
A Bahrain Monetary Agency (BMA) quarterly bulletin said end-June 1996 OBUs' assets were also down from the $62.50 billion reported three months earlier.
The BMA, Bahrain's central bank, did not say how many OBUs were operating on the island, but it said earlier there were 48 OBUs at the end of 1995.
There were 75 units in Bahrain at the start of the oil boom in the mid-1970s, and their assets peaked to $72.58 billion at end-1989.
Assets of 19 commercial banks rose to 2.57 billion dinars ($6.82 billion) at end-June 1996 from 2.50 billion dinars a year earlier and 2.56 billion dinars at end-March 1996.
Bahrain is the Gulf's main financial and banking centre.
